It has been revealed that bitcoin road back toward $80,000 may have a new catalyst after news from US regulators. CFTC has opened another door for crypto inside traditional financial markets. CFTC says regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin toward certain financial requirements. But what does this mean?

In a recent development, the guidance could help firms hold onto their Bitcoin instead of selling it to satisfy reserve requirements. It undoubtedly changes how regulated institutions can use BTC. This news comes as Bitcoin looks for reasons to reverse its recent weakness.

CFTC ALLOWS EXCHANGES COUNT BITCOIN FOR OPERATING COSTS.🚨 THIS IS HUGE !!!👉 Bitcoin enters clearinghouse reserves. pic.twitter.com/vP0NyuwLU3.

Industry observers note that released yesterday, it allows eligible firms to use Bitcoin, Ether, and qualifying payment stablecoins toward resources covering 12 months of operating costs. BTC and ETH face a minimum 20% haircut, while qualifying stablecoins face just 2%.

Bitcoin still has plenty of ground to recover, but can this news reverse the current bleeding trajectory?

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026.

Under the guidance, regulated derivatives exchanges, swap facilities, and clearinghouses can include certain crypto holdings in their financial-resource calculations. A firm holding $1 million in Bitcoin could count $800,000 after the minimum haircut.

According to recent reports, the allowance comes with a catch: crypto cannot satisfy the separate requirement for cash or highly liquid securities. Major exchanges and clearinghouses must still cover at least six months of operating costs with qualifying liquid assets.

Sources indicate that still, the change removes a barrier for firms already holding crypto. They can now put some of those assets to work toward regulatory requirements instead of relying entirely on traditional holdings. That could make Bitcoin a little more practical for firms operating inside the US derivatives market.

Bitcoin needs more than regulatory progress to climb 33%. The market has suffered heavy losses, and BTC remains well below its October 2025 peak above $126,000. A move toward $80,000 would require buyers to regain control and reverse the recent downtrend.

According to recent reports, the CFTC guidance won’t force institutions to buy BTC, but it gives regulated firms a reason to accommodate the asset. The timing is notable, with Bitcoin struggling around $60,000 and investors looking for signs that institutional demand could return.

A move toward $80,000 remains a tall order from here. But Bitcoin and its expanding role in regulated markets are giving us a fresh view to point to, even as the price and chart still need to confirm the recovery.

#99172. Why 16 MLSs want a united front against Compass in the battle over private listings

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (640 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Why 16 MLSs want a united front against Compass in the battle over private listings

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (640 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Compass International Holdings may have filed 16 separate antitrust lawsuits against 16 separate MLS, but according to court documents filed earlier this week, those MLSs are seeking to combine these lawsuits into one.
  • In a motion filed on Monday to stay the lawsuit Compass filed against it, California Regional MLS (CRMLS) told the court that it and the other MLSs Compass has filed lawsuits against have asked to consolidate or coordinate the pretrial proceedings for the various Compass v.
  • According to the motion, the MLSs have also asked to include the two declaratory judgement lawsuits nine MLSs have already filed against Compass in the SDNY.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Compass International Holdings may have filed 16 separate antitrust lawsuits against 16 separate MLS, but according to court documents filed earlier this week, those MLSs are seeking to combine these lawsuits into one.

In a motion filed on Monday to stay the lawsuit Compass filed against it, California Regional MLS (CRMLS) told the court that it and the other MLSs Compass has filed lawsuits against have asked to consolidate or coordinate the pretrial proceedings for the various Compass v. MLS lawsuits currently pending across the country in federal court in the Southern District of New York (SDNY). If the panel declines to select New York, the motion identifies the Western District of North Carolina and the Middle District of Florida as alternative venues for the consolidated litigation.

According to the motion, the MLSs have also asked to include the two declaratory judgement lawsuits nine MLSs have already filed against Compass in the SDNY.

“Compass has chosen to wage the same legal fight in courts across the country, creating unnecessary costs and the risk of conflicting rulings,” Richard Haggerty, the CEO of OneKey MLS, remarked in a statement. “Each of the 16MLS organizations are challenging that approach. We believe these cases belong before one judge, and we will continue defending the cooperation rules that ensure no brokerage gains an unfair advantage by withholding publicly marketed homes from the shared marketplace.”.

This request comes after Compass informed the SDNY court that it plans to file a motion to dismiss the declaratory judgement lawsuits or to sever and transfer each MLS’s claims to the district where Compass has brought its own antitrust case against that MLS.

After months of posturing and clashes over policies, the legal dispute between Compass and the MLSs kicked off in earnest this September when Compass sent letters to MLSs across the country demanding that they stop fining agents for publicly marketing office exclusive listings. Later that month, Compass CEO Robert Reffkin told a room full of MLS executives gathered at the Council of MLSs (CMLS) that he would sue any MLS that refused to give in to Compass’s demands.

Despite Reffkin’s threats, it was actually CRMLS that made the first move, filing a lawsuit in early October seeking a declaratory judgment that its policies on listing cooperation are “fair, procompetitive, and legally sound,” according to a manufacturer announcement. CRMLS has since been joined by New York’s OneKey MLS in this lawsuit, while MLSListings, Arizona Regional MLS, bridgeMLS, Canopy MLS, REcolorado, Hive MLS, and Doorify MLS have filed their own lawsuit, also in the SDNY, seeking the same judgements as CRMLS and OneKey.

In the midst of these lawsuits hitting the court docket, Compass filed its own lawsuit against CRMLS, alleging that its rule unlawfully restrict how homeowners and their agents can publicly market properties outside the MLS.

Recent findings suggest that roughly a month later, Compass reiterated those same claims in 15 separate lawsuits filed against 15 MLSs. MLS defendants in those lawsuits include bridgeMLS, Bay East MLS, Contra Costa MLS, MLSListings, The MLS-CLAW, San Diego MLS, Canopy MLS, Hive MLS, Doorify MLS, Arizona Regional MLS, Recolorado, NorthstarMLS, Houston Association of Realtors, Stellar MLS and OneKey MLS.

In an emailed statement a Compass spokesperson told HousingWire that the filing is “a procedural request  that does not change the substance of [Compass’s] claims.”.

“Each MLS applies its own rules, and the impact of those rules on agents, home sellers, and buyers is specific to its local jurisdiction,” the spokesperson added.

Industry observers note that it remains to be seen if court will allow the MLSs to consolidate their lawsuits. This is not the first time real estate industry defendants have sought to consolidate similar lawsuits. Several real estate brokerage defendants in the copycat commission lawsuits attempted to consolidate their cases, but their request was rejected.

Tech Report: Sometimes the most valuable data is the house nobody bought

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that want to price more precisely?
  • In a recent development, when agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds.
  • But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that want to price more precisely? Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers remarked no. Learn three steps to add failed listings to your next CMA.

In a recent development, when agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds. Look at what’s coming soon, active and pending. Adjust for condition, location, square footage and amenities. Figure out where our house fits.

But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.

It has been revealed that expired. Canceled. Withdrawn. Earlier in my career, I looked at these failed listings all the time. Then the market changed. When inventory became tight, and buyers were competing for homes, digging through failed listings often wasn’t necessary to determine where a property would sell.

Now the market is shifting again; pricing must be more precise, and I’m sharpening my approach by bringing an old tool back into my pricing process.

A sold comp tells us where a buyer noted yes, but a failed listing can help us figure out where buyers said no. And in a buyer-favored market, that’s valuable information.

Imagine you’re pricing a home, and the recent comparable sales range from $600,000 to $625,000. Then you expand your search.

Industry observers note that suddenly, you know considerably more than the sold comps alone told you. Other sellers have already tested the upper limits of pricing, and buyers responded. It’s essentially a series of pricing experiments someone else conducted for you — and they paid the carrying costs.

It has been revealed that one of the most interesting things buried in MLS history is the pricing journey. A property might show a final list price of $649,000 and an eventual sale of $630,000. Dig deeper, and you may discover this:.

$725,000 → $699,000 → $675,000 → canceled → relisted at $649,000 → sold for $630,000.

That’s a different story. The sale tells us what one buyer eventually paid. The listing history tells us buyers had previously rejected that house at $725,000, $699,000 and $675,000.

It also illustrates something sellers don’t always understand: Getting to the right price eventually isn’t necessarily the same as pricing correctly from the beginning. After months of market exposure and multiple reductions, buyers may stop asking, “Could this be the house?” They start asking, “What’s wrong with it?”.

Recent findings suggest that when I find a comparable property that sat for 90 days without selling, I want to know what did sell during those same 90 days. Sometimes we blame the market when the market was functioning just fine. Buyers were buying houses. They simply weren’t buying that one.

Industry observers note that maybe they chose the renovated house at $640,000. Maybe they paid $650,000 for the better lot. They may have even paid more for another property because it offered something the failed listing didn’t. That’s useful information when you’re sitting across from a seller who believes buyers just need more time to appreciate their home.

If buyers repeatedly toured the property and purchased competing homes instead, the market may already have delivered its opinion.

Industry observers note that this is where agents have to resist oversimplifying the data. An expired listing isn’t automatic proof that a house was overpriced, and a canceled listing certainly isn’t either.

Sources indicate that listings fail for all sorts of reasons. Sellers change their minds. Job transfers fall through. Repairs surface. Agents get fired. Sometimes a seller receives a perfectly acceptable offer and decides not to move.

Recent findings suggest that so, investigate. Call the previous agent. I might simply say:.

In a recent development, “I’m pricing a similar property and noticed yours was on the market last year. Is there anything you can tell me about the activity or why the seller decided not to continue?”.

According to recent reports, twenty-seven showings and no offers tell me something. Two showings in four months tells me something different.

There’s one more number worth considering: the cost of the pricing journey.

Find a house that started high, sat, reduced, expired, relisted and eventually sold. Then compare it with similar homes that entered the market closer to where buyers were actually buying.

Industry observers note that sellers often view aspirational pricing as a no-risk strategy: “We can always come down.” Technically, that’s true. But time isn’t free, and neither is market perception.

The next time you’re preparing a CMA in a shifting or buyer-favored market:.

We’re very good at studying success in real estate. But as pricing gets harder, I’ve found myself returning to an old habit: studying the failures, too. Sold listings tell us where buyers have been willing to say yes. Sometimes the house nobody bought is the one that tells us exactly where they started saying no.

Roxanne Hale is the associate broker of the Art House Team, brokered by RealtySouth in Birmingham, Alabama. Get connected on Facebook or YouTube.

  • Zeno Power has hit a major milestone in its push to build nuclear batteries for underwater use.
  • Industry observers note that the startup said today that it successfully demonstrated an electrically heated Stirling generator in a controlled maritime setting in Washington state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Alan Boyle on Nov 19, 2026 at 7:00 amNovember 19, 2026 at 8:01 am.

Zeno Power has hit a major milestone in its push to build nuclear batteries for underwater use.

Industry observers note that the startup said today that it successfully demonstrated an electrically heated Stirling generator in a controlled maritime setting in Washington state. The two-week demonstration produced electrical power outputs in excess of 20 watts, said Lindsey Boles, Zeno’s chief product officer.

“It’s a really substantial step for us — just solidifying our expertise in how to design these, and then confirming our ability to translate that into operational hardware that meets or exceeds what our customers need,” Boles told GeekWire.

Zeno is developing the power system with support from the Department of Defense as a follow-up to an initial $7.5 million contract awarded in 2023. The generator uses a Stirling engine to convert heat into electricity by cycling gas through heating and cooling phases in a closed cylinder.

For the recent demonstration, the prototype device relied on an electric heating element. Future devices will instead rely on heat generated by the radioactive decay of strontium-90, a radioisotope that can be extracted from spent nuclear fuel.

Nuclear batteries have been in use for decades, primarily for space missions ranging from the Apollo moon shots to NASA’s Voyager spacecraft and Mars rovers. But the batteries being developed by Zeno Power promise to be at least four times more efficient than traditional radioisotope thermoelectric generators, Boles stated.

In a recent development, boles stated the non-radiological test exceeded expectations. “There’s a difference between a design that works on paper and hardware that works in the field,” she said in a news release. “This is the moment our team has been building toward: proof that this technology works outside the lab.”.

According to recent reports, long-lasting nuclear batteries could be used to power undersea sensor networks or recharge autonomous underwater vehicles. “There are a lot of applications, especially on the maritime front, that we really want electricity for,” Boles said. “And we really don’t need a ton of it. But we need it to be really reliable, and we need it to be long endurance, and we need it to be self-managed. … I think of it like a slow Tesla supercharger on the seabed.”.

Retired Navy Adm. John Richardson, former chief of naval operations and a member of Zeno’s board of directors, called the recent test an “notable step toward undersea superiority.”.

Sources indicate that “Protecting maritime infrastructure and powering distributed systems at sea requires energy; energy that lasts for years, not days or months,” Richardson noted in a written statement. “As competition intensifies in contested domains, powered subsea systems will help keep us ahead. Zeno Power has steadily reduced risk, proven its technology, built a supply chain, and prepared to scale production.”.

Industry observers note that next year, Zeno Power plans to install a radioisotope heat source in its generator and test the system in a water tank under controlled laboratory conditions. If those tests are successful, Zeno will move forward with the first operational seabed deployment of its radioisotope-fueled maritime system later in 2027.

It has been revealed that the maritime battery isn’t Zeno’s only product. The tech giant is also working on a nuclear-powered heater system for spacecraft, with a demonstration on the lunar surface planned as early as 2028. Zeno’s broader vision is to provide long-lasting, reliable power on the moon and Mars, and in extreme environments on Earth.

Industry observers note that since its founding in 2018, Zeno has secured $105 million in private capital and has brought in $60 million in contracts with the Pentagon and NASA. The manufacturer has more than 95 employees at locations in Seattle, California and Washington, D.C., with the largest contingent working at its engineering headquarters in Seattle’s South Lake Union district.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp.
  • Epochal’s first offering is a cloud service called the Epochal Time Portal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:30 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc. launched today with $100 million in funding.

The capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp. He established Epochal earlier this year with two other xAI co-founders, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss. The organization’s staff also includes former researchers from Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC and Google DeepMind.

Epochal’s first offering is a cloud service called the Epochal Time Portal. According to the firm, it enables developers to train AI models that can predict future events. The service does so by providing models with access to historical web data from the past 30 years.

Sources indicate that if a bank wishes to train an AI that can predict quarterly earnings, it could use the service to fetch financial results from the first three quarters of 2025. It could then ask the AI to estimate fourth-quarter results from the same year.

Recent findings suggest that after the model generates its predictions, developers can compare them against real fourth-quarter earnings to check the model’s accuracy. They can make adjustments if necessary and then repeat the training workflow until the model starts generating accurate forecasts.

Industry observers note that the Epochal Time Portal features more than 1 trillion historical web pages on launch. Each entry includes a timestamp that indicates when it was created. According to the firm, its timestamps make it possible to track how a web page changed over time.

AI models access the content through a purpose-built search engine. It enables them to specify the time periods from which they wish to retrieve web pages. According to Epochal, its platform provides one-minute granularity for the most frequently updated pages.

Sources indicate that like consumer search engines, the Epochal Time Portal prioritizes the web pages that are most relevant to each given query. The difference is that it considers web pages’ creation date when evaluating relevance. If a query contains the term “Meta” but asks for pages created before 2021, the year Facebook Inc. rebranded, the Epochal Time Portal will not bring up pages that relate to the social networking giant.

Today’s frontier models can determine that they’re being trained on historical data rather than up-to-date information. For example, a model might compare the creation date of a web page to the virtual clock of the operating system on which it deployed. Such discrepancies can lower the effectiveness of training runs.

In a recent development, according to Epochal, its service mitigates the concern by deploying AI models in sandboxes synced to their training data. If a company is training a model on we pages from 2025, the Epochal Time Portal will run it on a Linux version from that year. It applies the same precautions to the software tools and programming language versions that models use.

The Epochal Time Portal is initially available in a single free tier with low usage limits. Epochal aims to follow up the launch by sharing the results of several AI experiments that its researchers have carried out using the service.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly 30 years after 6-year-old JonBenét Ramsey was found dead in her family’s home in Boulder, CO, the tragic case is regaining attention with the release of a upcoming Netflix limited series.

“The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey” tells the story of the cold case through a lens that seeks not to solve the mystery, but to tell the story of those who were involved—particularly as the 1996 murder occurred in a decade marked by high-profile crime.

The 1990s "ended with Columbine and started with the Menendez brothers, the Susan Smith murder, the OJ trial,” showrunner Richard LaGravenese noted in a statement. “I was fascinated by the challenge of doing something that was a murder mystery without an ending, without being solved.”.

To portray the effects of the media coverage that surrounded the case, the limited series will focus on Patsy and John Ramsey (played by Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen) as well as a group of local and federal investigators (brought to life by Garrett Hedlund, Will Patton, Shea Whigham, and Alison Pill).

“They all had different points of view for all different reasons,” LaGravenese mentioned. “It was an incredible story to tell from all these perspectives.”.

The Ramsey family’s former home was at the center of the case, and although a handful of interior and exterior shots in the series’ trailer strikingly resemble the recognizable Tudor, it has been reported that “The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey” was filmed in Calgary, Alberta.

Recent findings suggest that and while a few of the memorable details of the home—such as the black-and-white checkerboard tile floor in the kitchen—also make an appearance in the trailer, much of the home has been updated in recent years. Listing photos from 2024 show that the kitchen was entirely renovated.

The Ramseys purchased the home for $500,000 in 1991, and moved to Atlanta in 1997 following JonBenét’s death. They sold the home for $650,000 in 1998, with profits from the sale pledged to the JonBenét Ramsey Children’s Foundation.

The 7,240-square-foot abode changed hands again, for $1.05 million in 2004. Numerous attempts to sell the home since then have come to naught. In 2008, it was listed for $2.68 million; the price was later reduced to $2.29 million in 2009, $2.3 million in 2011, and $2 million in 2014.

Nine years would pass before the home was listed again, asking $6.95 million in March 2023. After a series of price adjustments, the property was taken off the market in February 2025.

JonBenét was found dead in the wine cellar in the basement of the home in the early hours of Dec. 26, 1996. Hours before her body was discovered, the family uncovered a ransom note in the home, which asked $118,000 for the return of their daughter.

Police determined she had been murdered in the late hours of the night on Christmas, and a later autopsy ruled the cause of death as strangulation.

In the following months, police investigated a number of suspects, including Patsy, John, and their son, Burke Ramsey—who were not cleared until July 2008, two years after Patsy died of ovarian cancer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, SHANGHAI, Nov. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Leekr Technology, a leading provider of intelligent chassis solutions, is accelerating its expansion into overseas autonomous vehicle markets, bringing its automotive-grade brake-by-wire technology, which has been proven in high-volume production in China's intelligent electric vehicle market, to low-speed autonomous vehicles. It offers DHB-P (Two-box: Decoupled Hydraulic Brake-by-Wire System) and IHB-P (One-box: Integrated Intelligent Braking System) to meet the braking requirements of autonomous logistics and sweeper vehicles.

Varying vehicle loads, emergency braking demands, and prolonged operating hours pose three major challenges for their braking systems. For low-speed autonomous transport vehicles, Leekr Technology's brake-by-wire systems dynamically adjust braking force based on vehicle mass and payload variations, in coordination with the vehicle control strategy, ensuring reliable braking under full load and smooth braking when unladen.

Recent findings suggest that the systems support active braking, with a braking response time of less than 150 ms, and work with automated driving systems to execute emergency braking commands, helping to reduce collision risks. Automotive-grade design, safety redundancy, and system self-diagnostics help maintain reliable braking during extended unattended operation. Its solutions have been adopted in series-production vehicles by leading autonomous logistics and sweeper vehicle OEMs in China.

Recent findings suggest that DHB-P (Two-box) is designed for mainstream OEM production programs. Featuring a fully decoupled hydraulic architecture with motor-driven active pressure generation, the system applies braking force in response to vehicle control commands without requiring brake pedal input. It supports integration with Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). The system supports human-machine collaborative driving and is compatible with both human-driven and autonomous driving modes.

Recent findings suggest that for vehicles requiring higher integration and more advanced active safety functions, Leekr Technology offers the IHB-P (One-box) Integrated Intelligent Braking System. It combines the electronic brake booster (eBooster) and Electronic Stability Control (ESC) functions in a single unit.

To meet the safety requirements of advanced automated driving, IHB-P can be paired with an independent Redundant Brake Unit (RBU). If the primary braking unit (IHB-P) fails, the RBU can take over braking control to bring the vehicle to a safe stop, meeting the braking redundancy requirements of SAE Level 4 automated driving and low-speed autonomous vehicle applications.

It has been revealed that leekr Technology is the first company in China to achieve mass-production deployment of an IHB-P + RBU redundant brake-by-wire solution in autonomous vehicles. In Europe, it will provide OEMs with customized brake-by-wire solutions and engineering delivery services.

Website: www.leekr-chassis.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The seesaw pattern for mortgage rates that’s been the story for much of the second half of 2026 reared its head again this week as rates for major loan types declined, reversing some of the increases from prior weeks.

At HousingWire‘s Mortgage Rates Center on Tuesday, rates for 30-year conforming loans averaged 7.53% — down 5 basis points from a week ago. Rates for 30-year loans through the Federal Housing Administration (FHA) dropped 7 bps to 7.30%, while rates for 30-year jumbo loans plummeted 25 bps to 7.62%.

Rates in the mid-7% range continue to weigh on homebuyer demand and affordability metrics. Last week’s application index from the Mortgage Bankers Association indicated that total applications were down 5% on a weekly basis. MBA data released Tuesday found that affordability is about 8% weaker than a year ago, even though it improved slightly from September to October.

In a recent development, “Higher mortgage rates weighed on application activity last week, with the 30-year fixed rate rising to 7.35%. Purchase applications were down 18% from a year ago, reflecting continued affordability challenges and softer homebuyer demand. The direction of mortgage rates in the coming weeks will be key to the housing market’s momentum heading into 2027,” MBA president and CEO Bob Broeksmit stated in a statement.

According to recent reports, dan Ribler, vice president of capital markets and strategy at national reverse mortgage lender Longbridge Financial, noted that the October jobs report should’ve sent rates higher. Nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000 positions last month and the unemployment rate remained steady at 4.1%, indicative of today’s healthier labor market conditions in relation to 2025.

Ribler noted that the jobless rate has been below 5% every month since September 2021, unemployment claims are lower than a year ago and the Federal Reserve‘s “own description is the labor market is very strong.” But strong employment trends have been overshadowed by stubborn inflation, which continues to run well above the central bank’s 2% annualized target.

In a recent development, “Inflation has been above 2% year over year 57 months in a row,” Ribler remarked. “The Fed has, by the way, under this administration, reiterated the 2% hurdle and that they’re going to be tough on inflation. They’re certainly talking the hawk talk, saying we’re going to keep inflation under 2%.

“But man, I don’t know about you, if my kid breaks curfew 57 nights in a row — and I say I’m going to punish you one of these times and I never do anything about it — at some point, he stops believing me, right?”.

It has been revealed that inflation is likely to prompt the Fed to raise rates next month. The CME Group‘s FedWatch tool reveals that a 25-bps hike in December is all but certain, with 96% of interest rate traders saying that the federal funds rate will rise to a range of 4% to 4.25%. It was last at that level in September 2025.

Much of the housing and mortgage industry headlines in the past week have cast a shadow over any potential market improvements in 2027.

According to recent reports, selma Hepp, chief economist at Cotality, remarked in a statement that existing home sales have fallen to their lowest level since August 2010. She also pointed to a Realtor.com analysis, which found that the typical repeat buyer will pay about $1,100 more per month if they choose to sell and move.

“A meaningful housing recovery requires rates to come down and, importantly, stay down long enough to improve affordability and unlock turnover,” Hepp said. “Until then, the adjustment is likely to come through weaker sales and softer home prices rather than widespread homeowner distress.

According to recent reports, “The number worth writing is the $1,100. That’s the jump in monthly payment a typical repeat buyer takes on just to move house. It’s the clearest explanation yet of why nobody is selling.”.

It has been revealed that upcoming home sales have been equally grim, with September’s seasonally adjusted annual rate of 676,000 sales representing a 5.3% decline from a year ago. Higher rates have also prompted homebuilders to remain cautious about creating more supply, with U.S. Census Bureau figures showing that single-family housing starts were down 3.2% year over year in September. Monthly gains in total starts were largely tied to the multifamily sector.

Industry observers note that “Challenging affordability has been weighing on the resale market. Newly pending sales fell 17% in October, the largest year-over-year drop since 2023,” Zillow senior economist Kenny Lee noted in a statement. “Single-family homebuilders have been navigating the same challenge. While homebuilders have been adapting to the softer market by offering concessions and building smaller homes, the 2027 spring home-shopping season could see a slow start as buyer demand continues to wane.”.

The relative lack of sales has weighed on mortgage origination volumes, with ATTOM data for the third quarter of 2026 showing that the roughly 730,000 purchase loans closed during that period were the lowest figure for any third quarter in 14 years.

In a recent development, refinance activity was also bleak, with the roughly 561,000 refis in Q3 down 19% year over year. Refi lending was down from Q2 2026 in nearly 90% of the metro areas analyzed by ATTOM, with the largest declines in major metros like San Jose, San Francisco, Dallas, Austin and Louisville, Kentucky.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

Make it 8: Connecticut joins first responder homebuying push

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.
  • The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing.
  • In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.

The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing. To qualify, first responders must have completed two years of service and purchase a primary residence within the community they serve.

In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.

Industry observers note that “Connecticut’s police officers, firefighters and EMS personnel dedicate themselves to protecting our families and communities, and we want to make sure they have the opportunity to build their own futures here,” Governor Ned Lamont said in a prepared statement on Tuesday. “By helping reduce one of the biggest barriers to buying a home, we’re investing in the people who serve our state and the communities that depend on them.”.

The program is part of Public Act 26-12, a state bill that aims to increase the number of first responders with a number of incentives, including college tuition reimbursement and improved labor protections.

Recent findings suggest that “The people who protect and serve our communities should be able to afford to live in those communities, and this program with help them do it,” Comptroller Sean Scanlon said in a written statement. “Helping the people who put their lives on the line for us every day buy their first home is literally the least we can do, and I’m proud to have worked with Governor Lamont and legislature to make this a reality.”.

According to recent reports, seven other states also have down payment assistance programs for first responders. Florida, Nevada, Georgia and South Carolina provide flat amounts, ranging from $10,000 to $35,000. Texas, Maryland and Ohio’s programs are percentage-based and offer assistance ranging from 2.5 percent to 5 percent of the purchase price.

The terms of each program vary. Most states forgive the assistance after five to seven years, but Nevada requires homebuyers to repay the funds within 30 years. And like Connecticut, Ohio also offers a 0.25 percent mortgage rate discount.

Recent findings suggest that “Homeownership offers more than a place to live. It creates stability, strengthens connections to community and provides an opportunity to build wealth over time,” CHFA CEO and Executive Director Nandini Natarajan mentioned in an announcement. “Through First Responders’ Time to Own, we’re helping the people who answer the call for our communities take an notable step toward achieving their own homeownership goals.”.

First responders often fall through the cracks of housing assistance programs because they don’t earn enough to afford market-rate housing but earn too much to qualify for federal housing vouchers.

In a recent development, inman explored this dilemma last September in a feature on workforce housing in resort towns like Jackson Hole, Vail and Tahoe. These towns can’t operate without first responders and other essential workers in the hospitality and retail sectors. However, rental and for-sale home prices have far outpaced what these workers earn, forcing them to commute long distances from more affordable towns or take on second and third jobs to survive.

The solution for some of these towns has been investing in workforce housing, which caps prices for households that earn between 60 percent and 120 percent of their area’s AMI. Most workforce housing is rent-only, but some states are extending the programs to include for-sale properties.

“I think the fact that workforce housing can be necessary or is a thing in the first place is really an indictment of the state of housing affordability in the country today,” Realtor.com Senior Economist Jake Krimmel noted. “I think it’s important to ground any conversation about workforce and affordable housing in that reality. It’s a market failure and a policy failure that someone could be a doctor, a teacher or another kind of professional and cannot afford to pay the market rent or own a home outright.”.

Windermere Principal Economist Jeff Tucker said workforce housing isn’t a panacea for affordability and works within an ecosystem of other housing and economic policies, such as upzoning, to create a more equitable market.

Tucker’s comments came a month after the Senate introduced the ROAD to Housing Act of 2025, and three months before the House introduced the Housing for the 21st Century Act. The bills were eventually combined into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which passed in June.

It has been revealed that “A broad package of necessary reforms to make more housing construction possible in much of the country is a really important component of a long-term solution to the housing affordability challenges we face,” Tucker stated. “Our current housing shortage took years to develop. So it’ll take years to build our way out of it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 19, 2026 at 9:54 amNovember 19, 2026 at 10:10 am.
  • Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut today in a record $81.3 billion initial public offering, with substantial financial stakes for the Seattle area’s two tech giants.
  • Sources indicate that for Amazon, the IPO is a paper windfall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 19, 2026 at 9:54 amNovember 19, 2026 at 10:10 am.

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut today in a record $81.3 billion initial public offering, with substantial financial stakes for the Seattle area’s two tech giants.

Sources indicate that for Amazon, the IPO is a paper windfall. The company started putting money into Anthropic in 2023, about $18 billion in all. At the $83 IPO price, its stake was worth about $161 billion. With Anthropic opening at $111.50 a share, that number was closer to $216 billion. The stock has since dropped below $100, which put Amazon’s stake under $200 billion.

Sources indicate that beyond the value of the investment, Anthropic is a major customer for Amazon’s cloud platform. The Claude maker has committed to spend at least $110 billion on Amazon Web Services through 2036.

In a recent development, for Microsoft, it’s more complicated. The Redmond company agreed in late 2025 to invest up to $5 billion but hasn’t disclosed the size of its stake. Microsoft is buying $1 billion of Anthropic stock alongside the IPO, one of seven tech companies buying a combined $26 billion. Anthropic has committed to spend at least $47 billion on Microsoft’s Azure cloud through 2033.

But Microsoft is also pitching its own AI models against Anthropic’s, and it has been working to replace Anthropic’s models with OpenAI’s in some Copilot features, The Information reported this week.

Industry observers note that listing Anthropic’s compute partners on CNBC this morning, co-founder Daniela Amodei named Nvidia, Amazon, Google and Broadcom, but not Microsoft. Whether it was a slip or something more significant, it was an interesting omission.

A historic debut: The offering tops SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO in June, and it makes Anthropic the first standalone AI lab to go public, ahead of OpenAI.

The five-year-old firm was valued at about $1.5 trillion at the $83 IPO price, on a fully diluted basis that counts employee stock and other shares not yet issued. The stock opened at $111.50, valuing Anthropic at about $2 trillion on the same basis. It has since traded as low as about $95.

Speaking before the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei noted Anthropic will slow the training and release of its AI models for as long as it takes to be confident they’re safe, and that going public only strengthens that resolve.

“We will not bend to either business nor political pressure,” he said.

In an interview with CNBC’s Andrew Ross Sorkin afterward, Amodei called the push and pull between growth and that kind of restraint “one of the central tensions at the heart of the company.”.

Anthropic is also a public benefit corporation, a structure that legally requires the manufacturer to balance shareholders’ interests with the public good.

What’s next: Both Seattle-area giants have hedged their bets. Microsoft owns about 24% of OpenAI, and Amazon put $50 billion into OpenAI earlier this year.

OpenAI, which confidentially filed for its own IPO in June, is still aiming to go public in 2027.

Anthropic’s co-founders and some of its biggest shareholders are barred from selling for up to a year under the IPO’s lock-up rules, and Amazon has remarked it expects a customary lock-up period.

Amazon will update the value of its Anthropic holdings in its fourth-quarter results, much of it through earnings, which means the paper windfall is likely to boost Amazon’s fourth-quarter profit even though it hasn’t sold a share.

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (469 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: FHFA raises conforming loan limit to $855,400 in 2027

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (469 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The baseline conforming loan limit will rise 2.71% in 2027 to $855,400 for one-unit properties in most parts of the country, according to the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA).
  • The $855,400 cap is an increase of $22,650 from 2026 and reflects slower home price growth tied to a weaker housing market and higher-for-longer mortgage rates.
  • Under the Housing and Economic Recovery Act of 2008 (HERA), the national “ceiling” for high-cost areas is set at 150% of the baseline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The baseline conforming loan limit will rise 2.71% in 2027 to $855,400 for one-unit properties in most parts of the country, according to the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA). Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will be authorized to buy loans up to that balance in the vast majority of U.S. counties.

The $855,400 cap is an increase of $22,650 from 2026 and reflects slower home price growth tied to a weaker housing market and higher-for-longer mortgage rates. The annual adjustment was 3.25% last year and above 5% in each of the prior two years.

Under the Housing and Economic Recovery Act of 2008 (HERA), the national “ceiling” for high-cost areas is set at 150% of the baseline. For 2027, that ceiling will be $1,283,100 for one-unit properties in markets where 115% of the local median home value exceeds the baseline limit. Conforming caps first surpassed $1 million in these high-cost areas in 2022.

According to recent reports, special statutory provisions apply in Alaska, Hawaii, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands. In these areas, the 2027 baseline loan limit for one-unit properties will be $1,283,100, while the ceiling will be $1,924,650.

“Due to rising home values, the CLL will be higher in all but 24 U.S. counties or county equivalents,” the FHFA stated in a statement.

It has been revealed that each November, FHFA publishes fresh conforming loan limits for the coming year. Increases resumed in 2016, after home prices returned to pre-Great Recession levels, a condition required by HERA. The statute also prevents the ceiling from declining in years when home prices fall; the cap only moves higher when national prices increase year over year.

This year’s adjustment is tied to FHFA’s third-quarter 2026 House Price Index (HPI), which tracks changes in average U.S. home values over the prior four quarters. Nominal, seasonally adjusted, expanded-data HPI indicated house prices rose 2.72% on average between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026, essentially matching the 2.71% rise in the baseline conforming loan limit.

Sources indicate that the latest limits expand the amount of mortgage debt that can qualify for conventional financing backed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Loans above FHFA’s limits are classified as jumbos, a segment still dominated by banks and portfolio lenders that set their own credit standards and capital requirements.

Sources indicate that mortgage lenders once again anticipated FHFA’s announcement and raised their internal conforming loan limits ahead of the official release to compete for volume. But they were conservative.

Rocket Mortgage was an early mover, lifting its conforming loan limit to $845,000 for single-family homes in 48 states in September. CrossCountry Mortgage adopted the same level.

Pennymac set its internal limit at $850,000, while United Wholesale Mortgage increased its one-unit cap for conventional and Department of Veterans Affairs loans to $847,440.

Breaking: Uncommon Thinkers: Andrew Redd’s audacious plan to turn ocean volcanoes into power plants

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 24, 2026 at 9:53 am.
  • Editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec.
  • Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 24, 2026 at 9:53 am.

Editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec. 10 at the GeekWire Gala in partnership with Greater Seattle Partners.

Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.

The dots connect, but the picture they form is anything but ordinary: bold in vision, fast in execution and enormous in potential.

Redd has next-level ambition, and he’s directing it at solving one of the world’s biggest and most urgent problems — adding renewable, massively scalable energy that can outcompete fossil fuels and reach the grid quickly enough to make a difference in the race against climate change.

According to recent reports, underwater geothermal energy has never been tapped in a significant way, but to Redd, the idea was irresistible. “It checks all of the boxes for our perfect future energy source,” he said.

He founded Endurance Energy on the north shore of Seattle’s Lake Union in January 2025, and this September the team oversaw its fifth deep-sea deployment. At a site 300 miles off the Oregon coast, its prototype system generated more electricity than it consumed. The startup has raised $63 million from investors and has roughly three dozen employees.

In a recent development, nate Bek, a principal at Ascend, praised Redd’s ability to attract “brilliant” talent in pursuit of his goal. The Seattle venture firm is one of the startup’s early backers.

It has been revealed that “I’ve been deeply inspired by what [Redd]’s building at Endurance and haven’t shut up about it since the day we met,” Bek remarked. “He somehow makes powering the world from the bottom of the ocean feel inevitable, all while remaining remarkably measured and transparent about the progress.”.

According to recent reports, for Redd, studying engineering and aerospace in college was so clear-cut that it wasn’t a choice at all. Growing up around Boeing, seaplanes, the Museum of Flight and the Pacific Northwest’s rich maritime industry naturally pointed him toward those sectors. He wanted a degree as expansive as his influences.

Recent findings suggest that “I didn’t really want to have to choose whether it was going to be boats or space travel or airplanes,” he said. “I just wanted to be able to do anything — keep the world as wide open as possible.”.

After graduating from Princeton University, Redd worked at Neuralink, an Elon Musk company developing technology that lets the brain communicate directly with computers. A year later, in 2021, he moved to Musk’s rocket company, SpaceX.

That was another no-duh decision, as Redd viewed it.

In a recent development, “I saw SpaceX as really the place to be, where early-career people are given the most amount of resources and responsibility, and that felt like the fastest way to learn and the most engaging possible scenario to be in,” Redd noted. “I wanted to be tossed into something that was a little bit crazy.”.

According to recent reports, redd joined as SpaceX was starting to build its first orbital Starship rockets. The program brought together passionate young people and experienced SpaceX engineers who served as mentors. Wild ideas were entertained and explored. Everyone was committed to the mission. It was just the experience Redd wanted, and he planned to stick around for seven to 10 years.

Then artificial intelligence started booming.

In 2024, the build-out of sprawling, energy-hungry data centers for AI was accelerating with no end in sight. At the same time, efforts to electrify transportation, heating and cooling were driving up demand for power. Redd saw these trends sparking a surge in new natural gas generation, locking in decades of carbon emissions.

He wanted to find a better way. He went into engineering mode, focusing on all the essential criteria for an energy source: it had to be clean, not dependent on intermittent sun or wind, capable of producing massive amounts of energy, readily deployable, subject to fewer regulatory hurdles than something like nuclear, economically competitive, and scalable.

Redd recognized the tremendous heat contained under Earth’s surface as a terrific source for renewable energy and realized that most of the world’s active volcanoes are offshore. The unknown was whether the rocky ocean floor would be suitable for geothermal wells, so he did some research and found publications from geology experts who stated the conditions would be “perfect.”.

“You can tell,” he said, “when there’s a moment in time that you need to go and reach out and grab something, and that was really my impression — if I didn’t start this now, this would never come into existence, or wouldn’t come into existence soon enough to make a meaningful impact.”.

Sources indicate that in launching Endurance, Redd was intentional about the culture he wanted to create. He was aiming for a multidisciplinary group of mission-driven employees eager to collaborate and learn from each other: top talent that would attract more of the same and make Endurance a place people were excited to work.

“The hardest part of an early-stage startup is recruiting,” Redd said, “especially if you’re a first-time founder.”.

The startup employs about a dozen SpaceX alumni, plus employees from the fusion manufacturer Helion Energy and the aerospace venture Blue Origin.

A strong team is key to Endurance’s success. That’s because, enthusiasm and passion aside, the startup faces steep engineering and economic challenges. The technology must withstand high pressure, corrosive conditions and mineral scaling inside devices, and seafloor machinery could be costly to repair. The systems will need expensive subsea cables to carry power to shore over potentially long distances. It’s a heavy lift.

It has been revealed that while the September sea trial didn’t go perfectly, Redd is happy with the results. The company landed its 3-ton power plant on the seafloor near a natural vent and produced net energy from it — albeit for only 8.7 seconds. Technical difficulties and a power-cable failure cut the dive short.

In a recent development, team members successfully operated the system remotely from Seattle through a fiber-optic network running along the seabed. Redd mentioned he’s grateful for access to the network, which is part of the National Science Foundation’s Regional Cabled Array and operated by the University of Washington.

According to recent reports, endurance engineers also drilled what they called the world’s first subsea geothermal well at a site about 5,000 feet below the ocean’s surface. The 2-inch-wide, 52-foot-deep well delivered hydrothermal fluid, but the flow was too restricted to run the power plant, sending the team to the natural vent.

Redd said there’s a lot of work ahead, but the team “made huge strides” in learning and in reducing the project’s risks.

Industry observers note that the company now is developing Leopard, its 2-megawatt generator. After testing the technology at the research site off the Oregon coast, Endurance aims to deliver power from a Leopard system in Tonga next year as its first commercial project. Subsea geothermal energy could ultimately reduce the island nation’s reliance on imported diesel and put the startup one step closer to its objective of generating terawatts of planet-friendly energy.

According to recent reports, “This was always the end goal,” Redd said. “Create something that is highly meaningful for the world.”.

Editor’s Note: Nate Bek of Ascend is a former GeekWire reporter.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 (SFF 2026), Huawei and CMA Small Systems AB (CMA), a member of the Huawei Global Financial Partner RONGHAI Program, jointly launched a National Payment Solution.

Sources indicate that frank LU, Director of Central Bank Integrated BU Solution Sales Dept., Huawei, and Maxim Neshcheret, Regional Director, Asia, CMA Small Systems AB, attended the launch ceremony. By combining CMA's software capabilities in national payment systems with Huawei's ICT infrastructure capabilities across computing, storage, networking, cloud, and data centers, the two companies aim to provide end-to-end joint solutions for central banks and financial institutions, accelerating the modernization of national payment systems.

Combining Strengths to Build Resilient National Payment Systems.

As digital transformation continues to reshape the global financial industry, payment systems are evolving toward real-time processing, greater efficiency, and enhanced interoperability. This evolution is placing higher demands on system performance, security, business continuity, and infrastructure resilience.

It has been revealed that with more than 30 years of experience in financial market infrastructure, CMA has extensive expertise serving central banks, commercial banks, clearing houses, and securities depositories, with core capabilities spanning RTGS, ACH, IPS, and securities depository systems. Huawei, drawing on its extensive ICT expertise, provides financial institutions with full capabilities spanning computing, storage, networking, cloud, and data centers.

Industry observers note that the jointly introduced National Payment Solution deeply integrates CMA's proven payment software with Huawei's highly reliable ICT infrastructure across computing, storage, networking, cloud, and data centers, providing customers with an integrated solution spanning payment applications and underlying infrastructure. The solution supports high-availability and disaster recovery deployments to ensure the stable operation and business continuity of critical payment systems. It also enables phased implementation and flexible expansion based on evolving business requirements. In addition, through the Huawei Global Financial Partner RONGHAI Program, the two companies have established a collaborative mechanism covering joint solution development, project delivery, and customer services. This helps reduce system integration and project governance complexity while delivering solutions tailored to the needs of customers in different countries and regions.

Deepening Partnership to Expand Global Financial Markets.

In a recent development, the joint launch marks another crucial milestone in the deepening partnership between Huawei and CMA. In 2025, CMA joined the Huawei Global Financial Partner RONGHAI Program. In September 2026, the two companies signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) during HUAWEI CONNECT 2026, further defining their collaboration in technology integration, joint solution development, market expansion, and customer services. The latest launch marks a further step in their partnership, advancing from ecosystem collaboration to joint solution development and market collaboration.

Rolled out in 2024, the Huawei Global Financial Partner RONGHAI Program aims to deepen collaboration with financial industry partners and accelerate customers' digital and intelligent transformation.

Looking ahead, Huawei will continue to work closely with CMA to deepen joint innovation and market collaboration in national payment systems, bringing their joint solutions to more markets worldwide and contributing to the modernization of global financial infrastructure.

So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1414 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.
  • Recent findings suggest that nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn.
  • Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a substantial decision to make in the next few weeks: take the firm’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.

Recent findings suggest that nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn. This is the fourth post in his series on “Life after Big Tech,” including the Seattle startup guide, laid off at 50 and VC funding is changing dramatically.

Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a substantial decision to make in the next few weeks: take the firm’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.

Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman declared the initiative in a memo on Oct. 26: a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below, which includes general managers and some vice presidents, in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. That’s roughly 27% of Microsoft’s 223,000 people. The organization expects 3,000 or fewer of them to accept.

Microsoft says the terms match its standard severance: base pay tied to level and tenure, continued stock vesting, a period of health coverage and career transition help. The severance package varies greatly based on the seniority or level of the employee and the number of years of service. Employees have until early December to decide and would leave by the end of the year.

The offer follows the Voluntary Retirement Program (VRP) that Microsoft extended to about 8,750 U.S. employees in April. About 30% of them, or roughly 2,600 people, took that offer.

All of this comes as Microsoft cuts jobs and changes the kinds of roles it hires for, while pouring money into AI infrastructure and data centers. At the same time, AI is reshaping the broader workforce, flattening management layers and changing what employers look for in new hires.

The worry I hear most is whether more layoffs are waiting on the other side. So the real choice is whether you leave on your own terms or let the firm decide for you.

I hear two questions from Microsoft employees thinking about the VEO: How easily can I get another job, and how hard is it to start a company right now?

Recent findings suggest that harder than you think, and it depends a lot on who you are. We are in the “low hire, low fire” economy.

There is MASSIVE demand for AI-native builders — product managers, data scientists and engineers — as companies adapt products to deal with AI. Companies are also in the process of adopting AI.

According to recent reports, one of the fastest-growing tech roles is the “Forward Deployed Engineer,” who implements AI solutions at customers. Security is also job #1 as models and agents get smarter and better at hacking legacy systems.

But it is very hard to be seen by recruiters and hiring managers right now. Candidates are using AI to customize their resumes to each job and using AI agents to apply, sending out 100 to 200 job applications per day. Recruiters are inundated with resumes and job applications, many of which are fake or inappropriate for the role.

It is critical to leverage your network in the job search, which can be hard if you have spent your entire career within one company.

According to recent reports, hiring managers have changed what they look for, too. AI fluency is becoming table stakes. The “process” of how you build/sell/market with AI is more important than what you build. Candidates are expected to show prototypes and proof of how they use AI tools every day.

It has been revealed that the jobs themselves are changing. A friend told me last month that he wanted an engineering manager role. There are fewer manager roles in the market now.

Industry observers note that AI has driven a reduction in management layers and a general flattening of organizations. The engineering team at a small AI company today is a CTO and a group of strong individual contributors. It is normal for managers to have 10 to 30 direct reports now, versus five to 10 in the pre-AI era.

Product management, program management and design teams are shrinking, as well, as AI automates certain jobs.

Hiring managers may view spending your whole career at Microsoft as a yellow flag. Microsoft is an iconic but unusual company. Almost no one else sells to and services customers the way Microsoft does, with an account executive inside nearly every large enterprise in the world.

The skills that get you promoted in Redmond don’t always carry over to a 500- to 5,000-person software company.

It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a company.

Software is cheap to build now. A product leader and an engineer using AI tools can ship in weeks what used to take a team a year.

It has been revealed that this cuts both ways for startups. Every good idea attracts a dozen competitors within months, and the big platforms will copy anything that works.

The true strength of a startup today is the ability to grow revenue swiftly and establish leadership in a beachhead market. The sales, marketing, product-led growth and distribution strategies are becoming the most critical parts of the business.

Recent findings suggest that the bar for venture funding is extremely high. Jason Lemkin of SaaStr recently shared data from ICONIQ showing that top “AI forward” startups under $10 million in annual recurring revenue are growing 900% a year at the median.

According to recent reports, one venture investor told me they advise their portfolio companies that if they aren’t on track for a $10 million run rate within two years, they won’t raise another round. Last week I spoke with an investor who owns part of a business with $4 million in revenue, growing 100% a year and losing $1 million, and it can’t raise.

There are three fundraising paths.

It has been revealed that 1) Think VERY big, raise a lot and grow fast enough to justify it. Build an incredible team pursuing an ambitious idea. Raise a large round based on the promise of becoming the next Anthropic, OpenAI or legal AI startup Harvey. Many of the most interesting companies are not software or AI-related, but are “deep tech” companies in defense, robotics, energy and biotech.

It has been revealed that 2) Raise a moderate amount of money from angels, family offices and nontraditional funds to build a business that has the ability to be profitable on one round of financing. You can control your destiny by building a company that doesn’t rely on the venture capital funding market.

Sources indicate that 3) Bootstrap and build a business that you own. Fund it yourself, grow it with revenue and get to profitability.

The question that most people are NOT asking is: What do I really want?

Before December, block out an afternoon and think about the last time you were happy at work.

It has been revealed that there are many frameworks for figuring out what you want in your career and life in general. I’m a fan of the Four Elements exercise. Write down three times in your career when you felt energized and effective. From those, work out what gives you energy, where you have the most impact, what culture you do best in and what your constraints are: money, kids, aging parents and how many more years you want to work.

On LinkedIn, I have seen examples of Microsoft employees taking the VEO to start their own businesses in property management, buy car washes, take time to recharge, spend time with family and travel.

According to recent reports, other employees are starting the job search in earnest but not taking the VEO. Many others are just getting back to work and doubling down on Microsoft.

Whichever way you go, start now. Start by aligning on your priorities and what you want from your career. If you stay, use the next year to build your skills with AI and to grow a network outside Redmond. If you leave to build something, decide early which of the three funding paths you’re on, because that choice shapes everything that follows.

The people I’ve watched land well after Big Tech had one thing in common: they knew what they wanted before they walked out the door, whether that was a new role, a manufacturer of their own or a year with their family.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) has approved the FICO 10T credit score model for use by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
  • It has been revealed that the staged rollout, revealed Tuesday, mirrors the VantageScore 4.0 timeline and is meant to give lenders, mortgage insurers and loan origination system providers time to analyze historic FICO 10T data, rework pricing and risk models, and update technology before a full transition, according to the agency.“The timeline below prepares lenders, mortgage insurers and loan origination system providers for the final step in credit score modernization: lender choice between FICO 10T and VantageScore 4.0,” the agency stated.
  • Bob Broeksmit, president and CEO of the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA), issued a statement of support following the announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) has approved the FICO 10T credit score model for use by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. It also released an implementation road map that would make FICO 10T broadly eligible and retire Classic FICO by September 2028.

It has been revealed that the staged rollout, revealed Tuesday, mirrors the VantageScore 4.0 timeline and is meant to give lenders, mortgage insurers and loan origination system providers time to analyze historic FICO 10T data, rework pricing and risk models, and update technology before a full transition, according to the agency.“The timeline below prepares lenders, mortgage insurers and loan origination system providers for the final step in credit score modernization: lender choice between FICO 10T and VantageScore 4.0,” the agency stated. At the Federal Housing Administration (FHA), VantageScore 4.0 and FICO 10T are expected to go live alongside the existing Classic FICO in January.

Bob Broeksmit, president and CEO of the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA), issued a statement of support following the announcement.

“We welcome this milestone as it moves us closer to the industry’s and FHFA’s goal of transitioning to true competition with two modernized credit score models,” Broeksmit mentioned. “We appreciate FHFA’s desire to provide a clear and transparent roadmap for this process. Given the industry’s experience with the just-completed adoption of VantageScore 4.0, MBA will work with FHFA and industry stakeholders to expedite the implementation timeline responsibly.

“MBA and its members will continue to engage with FHFA to establish meaningful competition for both credit scoring and credit reporting. Continued reforms to end the tri-merge requirement will further improve our credit reporting system and lower costs for borrowers. Today’s announcement is a critical next step.”.

The FHFA initially validated both FICO 10T and VantageScore 4.0 for use at the government-sponsored (GSEs) enterprises in October 2022. In July 2026, Fannie and Freddie released historical performance data for FICO 10T along with additional VantageScore 4.0 data, a key prerequisite for lenders and investors to back-test new score models and recalibrate credit policy.A FICO 10T pilot is expected to begin around December 2027. In this “launch and refine” phase, lenders will deliver a subset of loans underwritten with FICO 10T while FHFA, the GSEs and industry stakeholders monitor data quality, pricing and delivery performance.

Based on pilot results, FHFA expects upfront pricing grids and private mortgage insurer eligibility requirements, or PMIERs, to be updated to reflect the new score model. That step will be critical for secondary market execution and risk transfer structures that currently rely on Classic FICO.

It has been revealed that A limited FICO 10T rollout is targeted for April 2028, followed by a scale-up and transition phase that leads to broad eligibility around September 2028. During this final stage, FHFA plans to confirm industry readiness, fully implement Uniform Loan Delivery Dataset (ULDD) Phase 5, expand FICO 10T use across GSE channels and retire Classic FICO.

FHFA emphasized that dates after November 2026 are targets and are subject to change.

It has been revealed that in October, Fair Isaac Corp. said it will hold its wholesale mortgage price at $10 for a bundle of its credit scores for lenders and brokers enrolled in its Preferred Program. The $10 price is available through participating tri-merge credit report resellers to lenders that commit to FICO under the program. It covers both Classic FICO, which has been the mortgage standard for nearly three decades, and FICO Score 10T, the organization’s trended-data model.

FICO is also preparing a latest subscription-based pricing model for mortgage credit scores in 2027, sources told HousingWire.

VantageScore 4.0, by comparison, has been offered at 99 cents per score, or at no additional charge when purchased alongside a FICO score through Equifax, Experian and TransUnion, which jointly own VantageScore.

According to recent reports, bank of America Global Research, using data from Recursion, found that more than 170 lenders now pull VantageScore 4.0. Despite that breadth of use, only a small share of conventional loans are actually priced with VantageScore 4.0. In October, 20% of issuance reported a VantageScore 4.0, yet only about 8% of total issuance used the score model for pricing, according to the research.

Editor’s note: This story was updated with a statement from the MBA.
